neighbours.label: In sports game reports, the word ' the' or ' a' right after a verb for what a team or player does in the game, strongest when the lead, ball, puck or game changes hands (took the lead, stole the puck, lost the game, dropped a close game). Not the same verbs outside sports (take the bus, drop a glass, steal a purse, take tablets), nor other contests such as chess, elections or business deals. A sports setting can weakly lift an off-field verb (a coach taking the team bus, ~0.4).
neighbours.short: 'the/a' after a team's game move in sports reports
fire: Toronto took the lead early in the second period on a wrist shot from the point.
With two minutes left, the defenseman stole the puck at center ice and raced in alone.
The Hawks lost the game in overtime after a costly turnover.
Despite a late rally, the Tigers dropped a close game to their division rivals on Sunday.
Martinez won the ball in midfield and fed a perfect pass to the striker.
The visitors regained the lead when their winger headed in a corner kick.
Boston blew a ten-point lead in the fourth quarter and fell 98-94.
The Eagles recovered a fumble on their own 20-yard line late in the half.
quiet: The startup lost the contract to a rival firm based in Austin.
The theory of capital was not a matter of primary concern to economists in the late 20th century.
After the meeting, Toronto's mayor took the bus back to city hall.
A thief stole the purse from a parked car outside the station.
The startup lost the deal to a larger competitor in the final round.
The waiter dropped a glass while clearing the crowded table.
In the endgame, the grandmaster won a pawn and converted the position.
The incumbent regained the lead in the polls after a strong debate.

predictions: Blind test written by a second author from the label only. Expect most fire items above 0.3; risk: 'won the ball', 'recovered a fumble' may be weaker; the 'polls' lead twin is the hardest near miss.
